sentences.text: Thalassomedon is a genus of plesiosaur named by Welles in 1943, derived from Greek words meaning "sea lord".
It ranks among the largest elasmosaurids, with an estimated length of 10.86 to 11.95 meters and a mass of 4.4 to 6.8 metric tons.
This creature possessed a very long neck comprising 62 vertebrae, measuring about 5.9 meters or over half its total body length.
The skull measured 47 centimeters in length and held teeth that were 5 centimeters long.
Its flippers measured between 1.5 and 2 meters in length.
Stones found in the stomach area led to theories that they were used for ballast or to aid digestion.
Six specimens of Thalassomedon in varying states of preservation are displayed in museums across the United States.
Thalassomedon belongs to the family Elasmosauridae and its closest relative is Elasmosaurus.
This genus of plesiosaur appeared in North America about 95 million years ago.
The time range for Thalassomedon is the Cenomanian, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
